correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the actual Algorithm 4, whose GC operation removes the mean of the current gradient and whose stable-decay/Norm-Loss vector divides eta_t*lambda by sqrt(mean(vhat_t)) with NO epsilon while the adaptive update has positive epsilon. For a d-coordinate row, d>=2, f(theta)=0.5||theta-b1||^2, theta_delta=c1+delta q with q centered unit vector, clipping inactive under |c-b|<tau|c|, the centered first gradient is delta q and first bias-corrected second-moment mean is delta^2/d. The norm of the regularization displacement after the update is eta_1^2*lambda*sqrt(d)*abs(||theta_delta||-1)/abs(delta). This grows as a nonzero constant /|delta| if eta_1,lambda>0 and |c|sqrt(d)!=1; at delta=0 denominator vanishes with nonzero numerator. The adaptive step tends to zero because its eps guard is positive and numerator O(delta), so cannot cancel. Symbolic independent check for d=2,c=2 returned lim(delta*displacement)=sqrt(2)*eta_1^2*lambda*(2sqrt(2)-1). Assumptions ensure nonzero scheduled first rate; default code implementations with explicit guard are not accused.
